subtitles.en: So I break it down into two things. One is that the treasury cannot control the level of interest rates, I mean that's the short end, that's of course, that's the Federal Reserve, but they can control the curve shape.
subtitles.zh: 我把它分成两点。一是财政部无法控制利率水平，短期利率当然由美联储决定，但他们可以控制曲线形态。

subtitles.en: So I mean, the Scott Besson could decide not to issue any more 30-year bonds and buy them all back, and then he's fully controlled part of the curve. So from our perspective, he said that the curve is now too steep, he wants it to be if anything a bit flatter.
subtitles.zh: 比如斯科特·贝森可以决定不再发行30年期国债并全部买回，这样他就完全控制了曲线的一部分。所以从我们的角度看，他说曲线现在太陡，他希望更平一些。

subtitles.en: So we've put curve flattener trays on 10s, 30s, because that's what he's told us, but he's not going to control the actual level of the curve. So yields, I think, under what we've heard from Kevin Warsh, yields have gone up a little bit to start off with.
subtitles.zh: 所以我们在10年期和30年期上做了曲线趋平交易，因为他已经告诉我们了，但他不会控制曲线的实际水平。所以收益率，我认为，在凯文·沃什的讲话后，收益率起初有所上升。

subtitles.en: But also, have you seen that the curve is flattened on the back of what he said as well? Because he's putting in some sensible policies that take out a bit of the term premium, I think. So that's also going in the same direction as Scott Besson.
subtitles.zh: 但你也看到，曲线因为他的讲话而变平了？因为他推出了一些合理的政策，消除了部分期限溢价。所以这也和斯科特·贝森的方向一致。

subtitles.en: OK, so maybe some fed credibility has been restored a little bit. So you're more comfortable going maybe longer duration.
subtitles.zh: 好的，所以也许美联储的信誉有所恢复。所以你可能更倾向于拉长久期。

subtitles.en: And that's partly because there are other countries that are coming through. There are strong as the US. And the dollar was so dominant for many, many decades that there's only one way that that goes, some sort of erosion.
subtitles.zh: 部分原因是其他国家正在崛起，它们和美国一样强大。而美元主导了这么多年，所以只能有一种趋势，就是某种程度的侵蚀。

subtitles.en: So debatement, I've never been a big fan of calling it debatement. I think the dollar will just fluctuate over time. We've been long the dollar at the beginning of this year because the US looks as though it was a stronger economy.
subtitles.zh: 所以贬值论，我从来不喜欢用这个词。我认为美元会随时间波动。今年年初我们做多美元，因为美国经济看起来更强。

subtitles.en: It's been weakening just on the back of what's got best. And as said, but it's only been a couple of percent. So I'm not particularly worried. And I'm certainly not shifting all my money into gold or Bitcoin on the back of this. I think it's just fluctuations.
subtitles.zh: 美元因为某些原因走弱，但只有几个百分点。所以我并不特别担心。我肯定不会因此把资金都转向黄金或比特币。我认为这只是波动。

subtitles.en: OK, well, is equity still fair to say that's still your main overweight for most investor profiles? That's right. So on the equity side, we still like the earnings.

subtitles.en: Sorry, sorry. It was not to like about the earnings. They're crazy, aren't they? In terms of, even if you strip out some of those big one-offs, US earnings are still on a year-on-year basis, 20, 30, 40 percent picking numbers. It's just huge.

subtitles.en: So we still like that. And we still like the technology sector on the back of those earnings coming through. Whether or not they're sustainable, that's hard to say, but it's also a question in one year's time. subtitles.zh: 所以我们仍然看好。基于这些盈利，我们也仍然看好科技板块。这些盈利是否可持续很难说，但一年后也会有同样的问题。与此同时，你有强劲的盈利，而且市盈率估值看起来并不差，肯定不像互联网泡沫时那样。

subtitles.en: So you're comfortable still staying long on the equity side of the whole AI trade, but what about the credit side? Yeah, so that's the really interesting part of the AI trade because they are having to fund this investment. And I spoke before about Kevin Warsh, like maybe tapping the brakes on some of the investment to say, look, if you do too much, interest rates are going to have to come up.
subtitles.zh: 所以你仍然愿意在AI交易中保持权益多头，但信用方面呢？是的，这是AI交易中真正有趣的部分，因为他们需要为这些配置融资。我之前提到凯文·沃什，他可能会对部分配置踩刹车，说如果做得太多，利率就会上升。

subtitles.en: And at that point, it becomes more expensive for you to build your data center. And again, this is all very sensible policy making from my perspective. But if I'm lending this to the creditors of the AI, I have to also be comfortable that they will be able to make money on this. It's interesting that six months ago, I didn't want to lend money to the hyperscalers because the yields were too low, but now the markets moved.
subtitles.zh: 那时建设数据中心的成本会更高。在我看来，这都是非常合理的政策。但如果我要借钱给AI的债权人，我也必须确信他们能从中赚钱。有趣的是，六个月前我不想借钱给超大规模企业，因为收益率太低，但现在市场已经变了。

subtitles.en: I mean, if you look at Oracle's 30 year bond, which was issued the back end of last year for 100 basis points over treasuries, that's now more like 250 basis points. That yielding nearly 8% Oracle's an investment grade name, nearly 8% for 30 years, you know, that's starting to be interesting, isn't it? So there's always a valuation, and when you've got valuation and discipline, that's a perfect, that's a perfect marriage, I think.
subtitles.zh: 比如甲骨文的30年期债券，去年年底发行时利差为100个基点，现在大约250个基点。收益率接近8%，甲骨文是投资级，30年接近8%，这开始变得有趣了，不是吗？所以估值总是存在的，当估值和纪律结合时，我认为是完美的结合。
